newsitem.title: USA: Viasoft corrects Q2 basis for loss per shr.
newsitem.headline: Viasoft corrects Q2 basis for loss per shr.

text.p: Viasoft Inc said Monday it filed its financial report for the second fiscal quarter ended Dec. 31, 1996 that includes a correction on the number of shares it used to calculate its previously released loss per share data for the quarter and six months ended Dec. 31, 1996.

The loss was in connection with its $27.0 million write-off of purchased in-process research and development related to the recent acquisition of Rottger & Osterberg Software-TEchnik GmbH, viasoft said.
The loss per share was misstated due to the improper inclusion of anti-dilutive common stock equivalents in the weighted average number of common and common share equivalents outstanding, it said.

It said the correct number of weighted average number of common and common share equivalents for the second quarter and six months ended Dec. 31, 1996, is 17,045,000 and 16,938,000, respectively, resulting in a net loss of $1.42 and $1.34 per share for the respective quarter and six-month periods.

Viasoft said in a January 23 release that the number of shares used for computing per share loss for the second quarter and six-month period as 17,961,000 and 17,831,000, respectively, resulting in a reported net loss of $1.35 and $1.27 per share for the corresponding quarter and six months.

The company said the correction does not affect the company's previously reported earnings per share, excluding the write-off of purchased in-process research and development, of 15 cents and 24 cents for the quarter and six months ended Dec. 31, 1996.
